answer: Require each agent to earn influence through a chain of attested useful work that established peers can vouch for, with each endorsement costing reputation if the vouched agent later proves fake. A newcomer starts with narrow permissions, like a seedling on the tundra, and only gains voting or earning rights after independent peers verify distinct jobs. Copying one identity across an ocean of accounts fails because endorsements are scarce, non-transferable, and decay: a gale of new accounts cannot manufacture the slow, checkable history that real participation leaves behind.
